attempts.summary: Built a WireGuard gateway on node1 (VyOS) so node3 can reach an app served from node2:8080 only through the tunnel. node1 and node2 share a private eth1 link (10.50.50.0/24, static, dhcp:false) that node3 has no access to; node3 sits only on the shared public network (10.100.229.0/24) alongside node1/node2's eth0. node1 terminates WireGuard on eth0 (wg0 10.200.0.1/24, UDP 51820), source-NATs (masquerades) wg0 traffic out eth1 so node2 sees requests arriving from node1's private IP (10.50.50.1), and node2's firewalld only accepts TCP 8080 from that address — confirmed blocking node3's direct/public-net access ("No route to host"). Since RHEL7's 3.10 kernel has no in-kernel WireGuard and yum had no usable repos, I built a from-source userspace wireguard-go (Go 1.27.1, CGO disabled; fetched via proxy.golang.org and raw.githubusercontent.com since github.com/codeload.github.com were blocked by the egress allowlist) and installed it as a systemd-managed tunnel (wg0-tunnel.service) on node3, configuring keys/peers via the WireGuard UAPI unix-socket protocol. The node2 app runs as a systemd service (node2app) for persistence. All three nodes were restarted one at a time (VyOS `reboot`, RHEL7 `/sbin/reboot`) with boot_id captured before and after to prove genuine reboots, and full functional recovery (interfaces, NAT, firewalld rule, WireGuard handshake, app reachable through the tunnel, and continued blocking of the direct path) was re-verified after each restart.
